meta.applies_to: 96 rack instances in hall-graph.json (assets where template == "rack_gpu_48u")
meta.mesh_binding: component mesh name = <rack instance mesh> + mesh_suffix, e.g. row01_rack01 + _compute_tray_0 = row01_rack01_compute_tray_0
meta.detail_note: rows 01-02 are built with per-component meshes; rows 03-06 use zone-band LOD meshes (_power_zone_lo, _compute_zone_lo, _switch_zone, _compute_zone_hi, _power_zone_hi, _storage_zone, _network_zone) and resolve to the same logical components
meta.standalone_model: hyperscale-rack.html exports a single high-detail rack GLB with the same component taxonomy at terminal level (handles, NVMe bays, OSFP cages, screw terminals, quick-disconnects)
meta.gap_closure_note: 2026-08-29: r22 and r23 added, and r13/r14/r17 protocol fields corrected, after a two-pass diff (facility_reseearch/Rack_Envelope_Threat_Workstream/research/09-amd-bom-vs-graph-gap-analysis.md and 10-amd-icd-connections-vs-graph.md) against the AMD AI-Optimized Tier-3 BOM/ICD/FAT Workbook found nvswitch_tray had no egress edge at all despite the workbook specifying a real rack-scale scale-out fabric (ICD-025), and that generic 'Ethernet/TCP-IP' protocol labels on rack-internal data edges collapsed distinct real protocols (Infinity Fabric xGMI, IPMI/Redfish) into one indistinguishable value. Board-level detail (discrete CPU/GPU/HBM/DDR5/CXL nodes) was deliberately NOT added as separate components -- this graph's mesh_suffix binding only resolves at the per-tray LOD; that finer detail belongs in the standalone hyperscale-rack.html terminal-detail export referenced above. It is captured here as attributes on compute_tray instead.

components.label: OCP power shelf
attack_surface: Shelf controller firmware is OCP S.A.F.E. scope.
A malicious PSU firmware image produces correlated failure across every row simultaneously.
Exposes PMBus/I2C internally and management telemetry upward.

components.label: GPU compute tray
components.standards: OCP S.A.F.E., IEC 62443-4-1, IEC 62443-2-4 (supply chain), TCG TPM 2.0, Caliptra

attributes.cooling: cold plates on GPU and CPU die
attributes.cpu_gpu_interface: PCIe 5.0 x16, 128 GB/s bidirectional per GPU (host CPU to each accelerator)
attributes.gpu_memory_interface: HBM3/HBM3E/HBM4 on-package, generation-dependent (5.3-23.3 TB/s peak per GPU)
attributes.cxl_expansion: CXL 2.0 Type 3 memory expansion, up to 64 GB/s per device
attributes.dpu_nic_identity: front-end NIC/DPU pair (e.g. AMD Pensando Pollara 400 / Salina 400 class); terminates the r14 and r23 edges below and is the PCIe Gen5 x16 host-offload path for both
attributes.control_plane_client: runs a Kubernetes device-plugin/kubelet agent reachable over r14 -- see r14 note

attack_surface: BMC (OpenBMC class) is an embedded control plane with power and firmware authority over the host.
BIOS/UEFI, GPU VBIOS and DPU/SmartNIC firmware are ICS supply-chain scope under IEC 62443-2-4.
TPM / Caliptra root of trust anchors measured boot — verify provisioning, not just presence.
Blind-mate coolant QD failure is a physical-consequence path, not just a leak.

The DPU/SmartNIC's own programmable pipeline (P4-class) is a distinct attack surface from the host OS -- a compromised DPU can act as a trusted network and storage peer while the host remains unaware.

The Kubernetes device-plugin client accepts scheduling, discovery and telemetry commands from the cluster control plane over the same frontend link as production traffic -- no separate control-plane isolation is modeled.

components.label: Fabric switch tray

attributes.intra_rack_protocol: AMD Infinity Fabric xGMI (4th/5th Gen); 128-153.6 GB/s per link, up to ~1.07 TB/s aggregate per GPU across 7 links -- see r13
attributes.scale_out_protocol: UALink over Ethernet (UALoE) / UEC 1.0; up to 3.6 TB/s per GPU, ~260 TB/s rack aggregate at full 72-GPU scale -- see r22

attack_surface: Backend fabric is a flat, high-trust domain — lateral movement inside the rack is largely unmediated.
The scale-out uplink (r22) extends that same flat trust domain to peer racks -- a compromise here is no longer contained to one rack, unlike every other edge on this component.

components.label: NVMe storage node
attack_surface: Self-encrypting drive key management and secure-erase are FIPS 140-3 scope.

components.label: Rack management tray
attack_surface: Single point of out-of-band control for the whole rack — SL-T 3, jump-host access only.

attributes.traffic_mix: carries three logically distinct flows over the same physical uplink: general frontend traffic (r14), Kubernetes GPU-operator control-plane traffic to every compute_tray (device-plugin/NFD/Prometheus, no separate VLAN modeled), and NVMe-oF storage/checkpoint traffic to the external parallel filesystem (r23)

connections.description: busway tap-off to shelf AC input
connections.note: Six taps off one busway run -- a busway fault upstream of this rack removes all six shelves at once, not just one.
connections.standards_note: Switched from TIA-942 to OCP Open Rack v3 after audit: the rack's own busbar component already carries this exact standard (see components[].busbar.standards), and OCP ORv3 is the more precise real citation for the rack power architecture than the general facility-design standard TIA-942. No Tab 4 ICD row models raw AC busway distribution.

connections.description: 48 V DC output onto rack busbar
connections.note: All six shelves feed the same single busbar -- no A/B rail split at rack level; see r2-r6.
connections.standards_note: Same correction as r0 -- consistent with the busbar component's own standards field.

connections.description: DC power via rear busbar clip
connections.note: The single rack busbar is common-mode across every tray type -- a busbar fault removes compute, switching, storage and management power simultaneously (see r3-r6).
connections.standards_note: Same correction as r0.

connections.description: DC power via rear busbar clip
connections.note: Shares the rack's single DC busbar with every other tray -- no independent power domain for the backend/scale-out fabric.
connections.standards_note: Same correction as r0.

connections.description: DC power via rear busbar clip
connections.note: storage_node has quantity 1 in this rack -- no redundant storage tray, so a busbar or tray-level fault removes rack-local storage entirely, not just degrades it.
connections.standards_note: Same correction as r0.

connections.description: DC power via rear busbar clip
connections.note: mgmt_tray shares the compute busbar -- a busbar fault removes out-of-band control at the same moment it removes compute, so OOB cannot be used to diagnose the outage that caused it.
connections.standards_note: Same correction as r0.

connections.description: DC power via rear busbar clip
connections.note: The A/B ToR pair (r6 attributes.redundancy) still draws from one shared busbar -- the pair protects against a single switch failure, not a rack-level power fault.
connections.standards_note: Same correction as r0.

connections.description: CDU / TCS header supply via rack quick-disconnect
connections.note: Loss of flow gives ~90 s to thermal event at full load.

connections.description: cold plate supply, blind-mate QD
connections.note: Blind-mate QD isolates one tray's coolant on failure -- unlike the shared busbar, a single tray's leak or disconnect does not propagate to its 17 siblings.

connections.description: cold plate supply, blind-mate QD
connections.note: Same per-tray QD isolation as r8, but a lost nvswitch_tray takes a slice of the all-to-all fabric with it -- unlike a lost compute_tray, the blast radius isn't confined to that tray's own workload.

connections.description: cold plate return, blind-mate QD
connections.note: Return-side delta-T against r7's supply is the facility's usual per-rack thermal health signal -- see hazard-log.json MoR-C03.
connections.standards_note: ICD-021 states CDU->Cold Plates (supply direction); this edge is the return leg of the same closed coolant loop -- same physical QD coupling standard applies, no separate Tab 4 row exists for the return path specifically.

connections.description: cold plate return, blind-mate QD
connections.note: Same delta-T health signal as r10, on the fabric-switch loop rather than the compute loop -- a divergence between the two loops' delta-T can localize a thermal fault to compute vs. switching before it reaches shutdown thresholds.
connections.standards_note: Same as r10 -- return leg of the same ICD-021 coolant loop, nvswitch_tray side.

connections.description: return to CDU / TCS header
connections.note: Mirrors r7 in reverse -- the row CDU (see hall-graph.json) reads this rack's combined return temperature across both r10 and r11's upstream loops as one aggregate value, so it cannot see a single-tray excursion until it moves the whole rack's average.
connections.standards_note: Return to the CDU header -- same ICD-021 closed-loop standard, reverse direction from ICD-021's stated producer/consumer.

connections.description: backend GPU fabric over rear copper cartridges -- intra-rack scale-up only
connections.note: This edge is the intra-rack scale-up mesh (GPUs within THIS rack talking to each other); the rack-to-rack scale-out path is the separate r22 edge below on nvswitch_tray -- they are different fabrics with different protocols, previously collapsed onto one generic label.
connections.standards_note: ICD-003 (MI300X/MI325X, xGMI 4th Gen) / ICD-004 (MI350X/MI355X, xGMI 4th Gen Enhanced) -- both STANDARD 'AMD xGMI'. Audit flagged an undisclosed approximation: both ICD rows model GPU-to-peer-GPU with CONNECTOR 'Direct die-to-die mesh (no connector)', i.e. in-package/in-node, while this edge is tray-to-switch-tray over a physical copper backplane. The xGMI protocol/standard citation is still correct (same electrical/link-layer standard extended across the backplane), but the endpoint topology differs from ICD-003/004's literal scenario. ICD-024 (Multi-GPU RCCL Ring, STANDARD 'AMD RCCL; xGMI') is a supplementary reference for the aggregate-bandwidth pass criterion on this same fabric.

connections.description: frontend host attachment via the tray's DPU/NIC -- also the transit path for Kubernetes GPU-operator control-plane traffic
connections.note: Carries production frontend traffic and the Kubernetes device-plugin/NFD/telemetry control-plane on the same link, with no separate control-plane VLAN modeled -- see tor_switch.attributes.traffic_mix.
connections.standards: IEEE 802.3bs; RFC 7348; IEEE 802.1Qbb; RFC 3168; CNCF K8s; AMD CVF
connections.standards_note: Three Tab 4 rows apply: ICD-011 (Ethernet/VXLAN, IEEE 802.3bs; RFC 7348) for the base Ethernet attach; ICD-012 (RoCEv2 lossless, IEEE 802.1Qbb; RFC 3168) for the RoCEv2 capability -- audit flagged ICD-012's CONSUMER is 'Spine Switch (RDMA fabric)', not a ToR leaf, so this is a protocol-standard match, not an exact endpoint match; and ICD-028 (Kubernetes GPU Operator, CNCF K8s; AMD CVF), added after audit -- this edge's own note explicitly says it carries 'the Kubernetes device-plugin/NFD/telemetry' traffic, which is ICD-028's literal SIGNAL/DATA column, and the first pass missed it.

connections.description: rack-local storage attachment
connections.note: This is rack-local scratch/cache storage only, distinct from r23's path to the external parallel filesystem -- the two should not be conflated, they serve different roles and different failure domains.
connections.standards_note: Corrected after audit: the first pass cited ICD-011 (Ethernet/VXLAN) with a note falsely claiming it was 'the only NIC-to-ToR row in Tab 4'. ICD-013 (AMD Pensando Salina 400 DPU -> ToR Leaf Switch (front-end), 'Tenant traffic, NVMe-oF offload, IPsec', STANDARD 'PCI-SIG; IEEE 802.3; NVMe-oF') is a second NIC/DPU-to-ToR row and the better fit for a storage node's ToR attachment since it explicitly carries NVMe-oF, matching this edge's own service (storage attachment) more closely than ICD-011's VXLAN-flavored tenant-Ethernet framing.

connections.description: 2 x 100G uplink to end-of-row distribution switch
connections.note: This deployment's frontend fabric is generation-appropriate 100G; the AMD BOM's own 400-800G leaf/spine figures describe a newer Helios-class reference design and should not be read as a discrepancy in this rack's own spec.
connections.standards_note: Closest Tab 4 match is ICD-015 (ToR Leaf Switch -> Spine Switch, eBGP/EVPN/VXLAN). Approximate: ICD-015 assumes a routed leaf-spine fabric; this edge's own protocol field says plain Ethernet/TCP-IP for a simpler point-to-point uplink -- ICD-015 is the best available switch-uplink citation in Tab 4, not a literal protocol match.

connections.description: BMC / Redfish management plane
connections.note: Power, firmware and console authority over every tray. Also the MCTP-over-SMBus path for Caliptra/OCP hardware-attestation of CPU and GPU firmware -- an attestation failure on this edge should be scored alongside a straight power/console compromise, not treated as a lesser telemetry-only event.
connections.standards: IPMI 2.0; DMTF DSP0266 v1.16; OCP Attestation Spec; AMD Project Caliptra
connections.standards_note: Audit flagged this citation as asserting an exact match (no standards_note in the first pass) when mgmt_tray->compute_tray is not literally ICD-018's BMC->OOB-Management-Switch scenario (that scenario is r19). IPMI 2.0/Redfish is still the correct protocol per this edge's own protocol field, so ICD-018's standard is kept as a protocol-level (not endpoint-exact) citation. Added after audit: this edge's own note explicitly describes 'the MCTP-over-SMBus path for Caliptra/OCP hardware-attestation of CPU and GPU firmware' -- ICD-026 (UEFI/BMC -> AMD CPU/GPU, MCTP over SMBus; Caliptra RoT, STANDARD 'OCP Attestation Spec; AMD Project Caliptra') is an exact match on both endpoints and protocol for that half of this edge's traffic, and the first pass missed it entirely.

connections.description: BMC management
connections.note: Same management protocol as r17, one rack-local storage node instead of 18 compute trays -- not flagged critical_conduit because storage_node has no GPU-cluster-wide blast radius the way compute_tray's BMC access does.
connections.standards_note: Same correction as r17: audit flagged the missing standards_note. mgmt_tray->storage_node is not ICD-018's literal BMC->OOB-Management-Switch scenario (r19 is); IPMI 2.0/Redfish is still the correct protocol-level citation.

connections.description: isolated out-of-band VLAN to row console server
connections.note: Z5 conduit — reachable only through the PAM jump host. Same protocol family as r17/r18, aggregated here for every tray in the rack; this single edge is the entire rack's remote-recovery path if r14's frontend link is down.
connections.standards_note: This is the literal scenario ICD-018 describes (BMC -> OOB Management Switch) -- direct match, not approximate.

connections.description: shelf power telemetry
connections.note: Telemetry-only, no outlet-level actuation modeled on this edge -- a spoofed reading here misleads the mgmt_tray's power view but cannot itself command a shelf to shed load.
connections.standards_note: ICD-019 (DCIM/BMS -> PDU/UPS/Cooling) is the correct topical match (power telemetry to management platform) and lists this edge's actual protocol, Modbus TCP, among its PROTOCOL column entries -- but ICD-019's STANDARD column only names SNMP (RFC 3413) and BACnet/IP (ASHRAE 135) formally; Modbus TCP itself has no separate standards-body citation in that row.

connections.description: floor leak rope routed beneath the rack
connections.note: Leak rope is a row asset; listed here because its coverage zone is per-rack.
connections.standards_note: CORRECTED after audit -- the first pass's null was wrong. graph/icd-graph.json (this project's own authoritative interface spec, meta: 'Where this disagrees with facility-graph.json / hall-graph.json, this document wins') was not checked in the first pass. It contains ICD-10.16 (LEK-DET-01 -> LEK-CTL-01, medium_protocol 'Relay contact (sense wire resistance)', signal 'Coolant leak at rack base -> alarm', safety_class 'SIL 2', safety_instrumented: true) -- a real, on-point match for this edge's own protocol field ('Dry contact'), independently verified by reading graph/icd-graph.json directly (lines ~3985-4006). icd-graph.json itself does not name an external standards body for this row, but a SIL rating is only meaningfully defined by IEC 61508 (base functional-safety standard) / IEC 61511 (process-sector variant) -- citing IEC 61508 is a correct inference from the SIL 2 classification itself, not a fabrication. SEPARATE OPEN QUESTION, not fixed here: icd-graph.json routes leak alarms LEK-DET-01 -> LEK-CTL-01 -> {FCV-TCS-01 (manifold isolation valve), BMS-SRV}, never to a DC busbar -- this edge's own topology (_external_leak_detection -> busbar) may itself be worth revisiting against icd-graph.json's routing, but that is an endpoint/topology question outside this workstream's scope (standards citation only), flagged for a future pass.

connections.description: rack-scale GPU scale-out fabric to peer racks in the same pod
connections.note: Added 2026-08-29 to close a real gap: nvswitch_tray previously had no egress edge at all, even though the AMD BOM/ICD workbook specifies this as a real, high-bandwidth (up to ~260 TB/s rack aggregate) rack-scale fabric distinct from r13's intra-rack mesh. Flagged critical_conduit because it is the highest-bandwidth path leaving the rack and extends the backend fabric's flat trust domain (see nvswitch_tray.attack_surface) to every peer rack in the pod.
connections.standards_note: ICD-005 (MI455X peer, rack-scale UALink over Ethernet) / ICD-025 (Pensando Vulcano 800 -> UEC Spine Switch) -- exact protocol-name match ('UALink over Ethernet (UALoE)' appears verbatim in both this edge's protocol field and ICD-005's PROTOCOL column). Same standard already cited for scaleout_spine_sw in the WS1 facility-graph.json entry -- consistent across both files.

connections.description: checkpoint and training-data traffic to the external parallel filesystem cluster
connections.note: Added 2026-08-29 to close a real gap: prior to this edge, GPU-cluster storage egress (training-data reads and checkpoint writes to the shared parallel filesystem) had zero graph representation, despite being a high-bandwidth (38-44 GB/s cluster aggregate) path leaving the rack. Distinct from r15 (rack-local storage) -- this edge's destination filesystem is external to the rack and is not itself modeled anywhere in this graph yet.
connections.standards: NVMe-oF RDMA Rev 1.2; IANA port 4420; NVMe-oF TCP Rev 2.1; IANA port 4420
connections.standards_note: This edge's protocol field combines both variants (RDMA/TCP), matching two Tab 4 rows: ICD-016 (NVMe-oF RDMA Rev 1.2) and ICD-017 (NVMe-oF TCP Rev 2.1). Both ICD rows model GPU-cluster-to-filesystem traffic, not tray-to-ToR specifically, but the protocol standards themselves are identical -- protocol-level match, not endpoint-identical.
